latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Replication in respiratory, ocular, gastrointestinal, urinary, and hepatic epithelial cells with local shedding and cytopathic injury.
Type I interferon, IL-6/IL-8, and neutrophil-predominant inflammation producing fever, tachycardia, CRP elevation, malaise, and sepsis-like physiology.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Mucosal cytolysis and ulcerative epithelial injury
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Direct lytic infection of conjunctival, pharyngeal, intestinal, and bladder mucosa causing conjunctivitis, pharyngitis, diarrhea, dysuria, and hemorrhagic cystitis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Lower respiratory pneumonitis and alveolar injury
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Bronchiolar and alveolar epithelial infection with consolidation, capillary leak, hypoxemia, and possible ARDS.
Failure of cellular immune control from lymphopenia, HSCT, solid-organ transplant immunosuppression, congenital immunodeficiency, GVHD therapy, or intensive corticosteroid exposure.
High-level viremia and multi-organ epithelial/endothelial infection causing hepatitis, nephritis, pneumonitis, colitis, marrow suppression, shock, and DIC-like coagulopathy.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Urinary tract and renal tubular tropism
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Species B/C adenoviruses can produce hemorrhagic cystitis, ureteritis, and tubulointerstitial nephritis, especially in kidney transplant recipients.
Direct hepatocyte infection with nuclear inclusions, patchy or confluent necrosis, transaminase/LDH surge, coagulopathy, and possible fulminant hepatic failure.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Viral sepsis physiology and coagulopathy pressure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Systemic cytokine surge, endothelial injury, capillary leak, hypotension, vasopressor need, renal hypoperfusion, and DIC-like coagulation activation in high-burden disease.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Weaker under beta-blockade, conduction disease, or autonomic dysfunction.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Fever and CRP share upstream innate cytokine drive.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Can be blunted by profound immunosuppression or corticosteroids.
Modified by baseline lung disease and respiratory support.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Lower saturation increases the hazard of invasive ventilation.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Depends on work of breathing, mental status, and available noninvasive support.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Escalating oxygen support is a clinical marker of evolving ARDS.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Only applies when hypoxemia is from lower respiratory disease.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: ARDS is a major proximate cause of death in severe adenovirus pneumonia.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Higher if shock, DIC, AKI, or immunosuppression coexist.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Rising creatinine indicates ongoing adenovirus nephritis, shock kidney, obstruction, or nephrotoxic injury.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Interpret against baseline kidney function and transplant status.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: AKI worsens prognosis and constrains antiviral choices.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Stronger in shock, transplant allograft dysfunction, or when cidofovir is needed.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Rapidly rising AST reflects expanding hepatic necrosis.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Most meaningful when ALT/LDH also rise and other causes are unsupported.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: INR elevation signals hepatic synthetic failure or systemic coagulopathy.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Anticoagulation and vitamin K deficiency must be interpreted as context.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Fulminant hepatic failure is a direct mortality pathway.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Especially relevant after HSCT or profound T-cell immunosuppression.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: DIC-like coagulopathy increases bleeding, thrombosis, shock, and organ failure risk.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Most relevant in fulminant pneumonia, shock, or liver failure.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Lower lymphocyte count impairs viral clearance and permits higher viral load.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Strongest after HSCT, solid-organ transplant, or congenital T-cell defects.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: High and persistent blood viral load marks disseminated disease and poor immune control.
axis_couplings.conditionality: Blood viral load is more prognostic than isolated urine or respiratory shedding.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Respiratory support has most benefit when hypoxemia or work of breathing is present.

side_effects.interpretation: Invasive ventilation increases nosocomial pneumonia risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supportive oxygen, high-flow or noninvasive support, intubation, lung-protective ventilation, prone positioning, and ECMO-level referral when needed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Restoring cellular immunity is central to viral clearance in transplant-associated adenovirus.

side_effects.interpretation: Solid-organ transplant recipients can reject if immunosuppression is reduced too aggressively.
HSCT recipients can develop or worsen GVHD as immune suppression is reduced.

treatments.context_specific_role: Decrease antimetabolite or calcineurin/steroid intensity when viral disease threatens organ function and graft/GVHD risk allows.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cidofovir is generally reserved for progressive, disseminated, or high-risk transplant adenovirus rather than ordinary self-limited disease.
Cidofovir nephrotoxicity can worsen kidney injury, especially in allograft nephritis or baseline CKD.

side_effects.interpretation: Dose-limiting proximal tubular nephrotoxicity; probenecid and hydration reduce but do not eliminate risk.
Myelosuppression risk in transplant or marrow-toxic contexts.

treatments.context_specific_role: Antiviral option for progressive or disseminated adenovirus, especially in transplant recipients, with renal-protective measures and viral-load monitoring.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Brincidofovir is less nephrotoxic than cidofovir but access and evidence vary.

side_effects.interpretation: Gastrointestinal toxicity can mimic or worsen adenovirus enteritis.

treatments.context_specific_role: Considered only where access and specialist infectious disease guidance support use.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Adoptive T-cell therapy addresses the cellular immune deficit that drives refractory HSCT-associated adenovirus.

side_effects.interpretation: Alloreactive or inflammatory toxicity may occur depending on product and host context.

treatments.context_specific_role: Specialist therapy for refractory or high-risk adenovirus in HSCT/profound T-cell deficiency settings.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: IVIG is supportive in selected immunodeficient hosts but does not replace cellular immunity.

side_effects.interpretation: IVIG can worsen fluid status in renal or cardiac dysfunction.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunctive replacement or immune support when hypogammaglobulinemia or transplant immune deficiency is present.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal support matters most when nephritis, shock kidney, obstruction, or nephrotoxic risk is active.

treatments.context_specific_role: Hydration, renal-dose adjustment, nephrotoxin avoidance, obstruction evaluation, and renal replacement therapy when indicated.

type_3_4_7_14_21_or_species_b_11_34_35.trajectory_modulation: Respiratory virulent types increase pneumonia/ARDS risk; species B urinary types increase cystitis/nephritis risk.

risk_factors.factor: Delayed recognition after progression to organ failure

supportive_care: Droplet/contact precautions and outbreak control for suspected respiratory or conjunctival adenovirus.
Assess oxygenation, work of breathing, chest imaging, and need for ICU-level respiratory support when dyspnea or low oxygen saturation is present.
Blood, respiratory, urine, stool, and tissue adenovirus PCR should be interpreted by compartment; blood viremia is more concerning for disseminated disease than isolated shedding.
In transplant recipients, monitor serial adenovirus viral load, lymphocyte count, renal function, liver tests, and allograft symptoms.
Reduce immunosuppression only with transplant/hematology input because GVHD flare or allograft rejection can follow.
Use renal-protective measures and dose review before cidofovir; avoid concurrent nephrotoxins where possible.
Trend AST, ALT, LDH, bilirubin, INR, platelet count, and fibrinogen when hepatitis, shock, or DIC-like physiology is suspected.
Evaluate dysuria, hematuria, urinary retention, and allograft tenderness with urinalysis, culture, imaging for obstruction, and biopsy when rejection or viral nephritis must be distinguished.
Avoid interpreting PCR, IHC, culture, or viral typing as ordinary presentation evidence in ranking; preserve them as confirmatory virology/pathology context.
Provide organ support for ARDS, shock, AKI, and hepatic failure while disease-directed options take effect or immune recovery occurs.
